project.name: watchlist-triage
project.objective: Triage sanctions/PEP name-match alerts from a frozen synthetic world: recommend close or escalate with cited evidence, human-approved, measured on zero missed planted true matches.

plan_approval.reason: I approve this plan because it follows a logical order, from creating a synthetic world to building a baseline agent and measuring it. Every task is linked to spec requirements with a test that proves it is done. Higher-risk tasks must go through independent review and my sign-off, and I can plan later upgrades after the baseline, based on real failures.

approval.reason: I'm comfortable building against this spec because it clearly defines what the system must do, how success will be checked, and what is out of scope. The rules for setting targets and calculating metrics are settled, and the actual target numbers will be set after the baseline milestone.

decisions.title: Specification v3.1 accepted after independent review.
decisions.text: Three Codex review rounds plus a two-item closure check. Round 1 BLOCK, 17 findings, all adopted (raw-data minimization and reviewer identity narrowed). Round 2 BLOCK, 13 findings, all fixed. Round 3 BLOCK on 2 partial fixes with no new blockers, fixed in v3.1. Closure check APPROVE. Owner decisions: D1 contradictory evidence is never a clear false positive; D2 hash chain plus a checkpoint in public git history; D3 a pre-registered fresh-seed world; D4 world mix of 30 TRUE_MATCH, 30 AMBIGUOUS_BY_DESIGN and 540 CLEAR_FALSE_POSITIVE; D5 round 3 limited to closure. Review texts are in docs/reviews/. Limitation: reviewer verdicts were pasted by the owner and are not cryptographically attested. Approval covers commit 7fba5db, SPEC.md hash 5dfdbe19a96cc04be14889b0fed6a25ad73a7f929e3c7375ebf37990bc4bc494. Round 2 marked 11 round-1 items as partially fixed; their remaining gaps were carried into round-2 findings, and only QA_SAMPLING and buyer scope were re-checked individually. The Kim and Yang 2024 citation was verified by the owner against the publisher page on 2026-10-07.

decisions.title: Only date of birth or ID number can rule out identity
decisions.text: I decided the agent can close an alert only when date of birth or ID number conflicts, no decisive identifier agrees, and nothing links the customer to the listed person. Nationality is weak evidence because it can be wrong or change. If I let it close alerts, the agent could miss a real match, and a missed match costs more than an extra escalation. So a nationality mismatch alone never closes an alert or sets its label.

decisions.title: Synthetic world design choices for T02
decisions.text: I chose how the synthetic world is built. Names come from small fictional name-part lists in the repo, so there is no library and no data licence issue. Variants use Latin script only, which I state as a known limit. The generated world is committed with a reference hash, and a drift check regenerates it in a temp folder. The matcher compares names only and allows a one-character spelling difference per name part. The world has 15 injection alerts, 5 per label, each with a control twin outside the 600. ID numbers use an obviously synthetic format so they can never match a real ID. Of the 540 clear false positives, 30 per hard family are hard cases and the rest are plain. Ambiguous alerts are 6 per family.

decisions.title: Former PEP beyond 12 months is decided by the PEP section
decisions.text: I found that two rubric sentences disagreed. One said a confirmed identity is TRUE_MATCH. The PEP section said a confirmed former PEP more than 12 months out of office with no continuing-risk snippet is AMBIGUOUS. I chose to amend the rubric to version 1.1 so the PEP section wins for that case, because it is the more specific rule and the public rubric should not contradict itself.

decisions.title: State the hard-case TRUE_MATCH rule in the rubric
decisions.text: Independent review showed six true matches rely on a hard-case exception the rubric never spelled out. I chose to write the rule down in rubric version 1.2: exactly one agreeing decisive identifier, no decisive conflict, and a snippet linking the customer to the listed person is a TRUE_MATCH. A snippet adds risk here and never lowers it. I also clarified four label-affecting points so two readers cannot apply them differently.
decisions.source: owner decision in chat, 2026-10-09, after Codex review round 1

decisions.title: Fixes after the first independent review of the world
decisions.text: The independent review found shortcuts in the world and gaps in the tests. I chose to spread the injected instructions evenly across labels, keep twin copies out of the agent loader and place injected notes at random positions, make watchlist group sizes and snippet counts independent of the label, give relationship records the related politician leaving date, and make the tests check that evidence matches the customer and watchlist records. I accepted the remaining limits and wrote them down.
decisions.source: owner decision in chat, 2026-10-09, after Codex review round 1

decisions.title: Fixes after the second independent review of the world
decisions.text: The second review generated worlds from other seeds and found labels that the visible text did not support, and injected texts that still predicted the label. I chose to use five injected texts, each used once per label, to rewrite the note templates so the text itself meets the rubric wording, to validate dates and tighten the loader, and to correct the design note. I accepted the remaining cues, such as neutral notes appearing mostly on clear false positives, as written limits.
decisions.source: owner decision in chat, 2026-10-09, after Codex review round 2

decisions.title: Codex round 3 approved T02 world
decisions.text: Codex round 3 (read-only, own classifier, three fresh seeds 7, 271, 8675309) returned APPROVE. All five round 2 defects fixed. Residual cues are minor and disclosed in the design note: neutral notes about 95 percent clear false positives versus a 90 percent base rate, injection presence rule 545 of 600 versus 540 of 600 for always closing. Loader isolation covers the loader path only; harness isolation is T06. Ablation without neutral notes planned.

decisions.title: CI drift check deferred to wave 2
decisions.text: Anchor artifact A.13.2 (CI check that the frozen world is byte-identical on every commit) is not covered by any wave-1 task and no CI workflow exists. Owner chose to add it as a small task at the wave-2 reopen, not before T03. The world hash is frozen at b77a6804a52b1d41650e250a31ff64a701b1d315a674a1f1242d93cb6b15c9b0, so drift in the meantime is covered by the existing determinism tests run locally. Overturn if the world files change before wave 2.

decisions.title: T03 framing design (D1-D7)
decisions.text: Owner decisions for T03 framings, 2026-10-09. D1: Framing 1 is the alert exactly as in the world (identity). Framings 2 and 3 are each transformed in all three ways (field order, name format, snippet wording) and the three must differ from each other. D2: Snippet wording is changed by a fixed, hand-written table with no model calls; the owner reviews the whole set once and the review is recorded later. D3: Framings are produced by a pure function in a new package at the repo root (framings/, stdlib only, same style as worldgen/); nothing is written into data/world/ and the world hash must not change. D4: The five injected attack texts are byte-identical in every framing. D5: Alternate wordings are per note type (tag): 5 tags x 2 alternates (one for framing 2, one for framing 3) = 10 lines; tags are neutral, identity_link, continuing_risk, relationship, contradicts. D6: Names are reordered and re-punctuated only, by position, never guessing given or family name; titles and accents stay as written. Framing 2 is 'TITLE LAST, rest': last non-title token upper-cased, comma, remaining non-title tokens in original order, title stays first and gets a trailing dot if it has none. Framing 3: last non-title token moved to the front, no comma, no upper-casing, title stays first and loses its trailing dot if it has one. Aliases use the same format. If upper-casing would change the normalised letters of any name, stop and report instead of working around it. D7: Field order is fixed per framing; blocks are the three kinds customer_field, watchlist_field, snippet. Framing 2: watchlist block, customer block, then notes, fields inside each block keep their order. Framing 3: notes first, then the customer block in reverse field order, then the watchlist block in reverse field order. Rules: evidence IDs never change. The same function applies to the twin alerts, read only via worldgen.harness_twins. The framing code never reads hidden/; it finds a snippet's note type by rendering the templates in worldgen.snippets with the alert's own names and comparing text; a snippet matching no template is left unchanged and must be one of the five injected texts, otherwise an error is raised; a snippet matching more than one template raises an error. Names inside rewritten notes use the same name format as that framing's name fields. Deterministic: no randomness, no clock, no environment lookups. Injected texts, dates, ID numbers, nationalities, addresses, pep_status, office, relationship fields and every date field are byte-identical across framings.

decisions.title: Neutral alternates must be content-free
decisions.text: Owner chose option A (2026-10-09): the two neutral alternates carry no identity, risk, relationship or all-clear content; they are administrative notes in the style of the five original neutral wordings. The other eight alternates are approved as drafted.

decisions.title: Neutral alternates keep the originals' reassurance level
decisions.text: Supersedes DEC-T03-NEUTRAL-WORDING. Owner chose option B (2026-10-09): the five original neutral wordings already carry mild reassurance, so the two neutral alternates restore that level to keep framings meaning-equal. The reassurance cue is a property of the T02 world and is measured by the planned neutral-note ablation, not hidden in T03.

decisions.title: Owner review of the T03 wording-transformation set (AC-23)
decisions.text: I read all ten alternate wordings in docs/framings/wording-set.md against the five originals of each note type. Each alternate keeps what the rubric needs for its type. I accept that specifics such as spouse versus sibling, or the kind of conflict in a contradicting note, are generalised in framings 2 and 3, so a verdict change there could partly come from lost detail; I will state this as a limit. The neutral alternates keep the same mild reassurance as the originals (decision DEC-T03-NEUTRAL-REVERSED), so the three framings carry equal meaning. The five injected texts are not reworded in any framing.

decisions.title: Wording differences apply only where a note exists (D10)
decisions.text: D10 = A: wording differences apply only where a note exists. Every alert must differ across the three framings in field order and name format; every alert that has at least one note must also differ in wording. 280 of 615 alerts and twins have no note; this is a stated limit, not a gap. AC-23 asks only for property tests and the owner's review.

decisions.title: Alternates are written per original wording (D11)
decisions.text: D11 = B: alternates are written per original wording, not per note type: 25 originals x 2 = 50 alternates (one for framing 2, one for framing 3). This supersedes D5 (per-type), DEC-T03-NEUTRAL-WORDING, DEC-T03-NEUTRAL-REVERSED and the earlier DEC-T03-WORDING-REVIEW, which now needs a fresh owner review. Reason: Codex round 1 showed one line per type changes facts (neutral note gained a check and a follow-up outcome; a passport nationality difference became a generic different-individual note).

decisions.title: Owner review of the per-original wording set (AC-23)
decisions.text: Supersedes DEC-T03-WORDING-REVIEW. I read all fifty alternate wordings in docs/framings/wording-set.md against their 25 originals. Each alternate keeps the facts of its original: the source, the document or relationship, and the specifics such as passport nationality or the kind of family tie. Each keeps the original’s direction and its level of reassurance, and adds no new check, outcome or instruction. Each also carries its original’s key-fact words. I accept the limits: the checks are keyword-based and cannot prove meaning is identical, 8 of the 25 originals do not occur in the frozen world, and 280 of 615 alerts have no note to reword. The five injected texts are not reworded in any framing.

decisions.title: FR-21 reading: wording differs only where a note exists (amends D1)
decisions.text: Owner decision 12, amends D1 (DEC-T03-FRAMINGS-DESIGN). D1 said framings 2 and 3 are each transformed "in all three ways" (field order, name format, snippet wording). Per D10 (DEC-T03-NOSNIPPET), wording differs only where a note exists: 335 of the 615 bundles (600 alerts and 15 twins) carry a note and 280 have none. So framings 2 and 3 always differ from the original and from each other in field order and name format, and in wording wherever a note exists. This is the owner's reading of FR-21. SPEC.md is not changed. A spec clarification is carried as an open item to the wave-2 reopen.
decisions.source: owner decision 12; Codex round 2 findings, docs/reviews/t03-review-round-2.md

tasks.outcome: Produce an approved, implementation-ready product specification

evidence.reason: I'm comfortable building against this spec because it clearly defines what the system must do, how success will be checked, and what is out of scope. The rules for setting targets and calculating metrics are settled, and the actual target numbers will be set after the baseline milestone.

tasks.next_action: Interview the human, record durable context, and replace every placeholder in SPEC.md.

tasks.outcome: Write the synthetic-world adjudication rubric: the three labels, what evidence is sufficient to close, PEP status and date rules, identifier-conflict weighting, the supporting evidence key and record provenance fields, committed before any generator code.

Build the deterministic world generator and matcher: 600 labelled alerts (30 TRUE_MATCH, 30 AMBIGUOUS_BY_DESIGN, 540 CLEAR_FALSE_POSITIVE), five families with 6 TRUE_MATCH per primary family, injection alerts with control twins outside the 600, provenance on every record, byte-identical regeneration, and secret scanning across the repository.
Produce three meaning-preserving framings per alert, with property tests for the structured transformations and a fixed wording-transformation set recorded as reviewed by the owner.

Provide one model-agnostic interface with a stub model selected only by configuration, and enforce that the agent process can reach nothing except the model interface. Covers the network part of AC-11 and the stub-model part of AC-14.

Build the naive baseline agent: CLOSE or ESCALATE with a written reason and cited evidence IDs, rejection of results without them, escalation on unclear evidence, model and output faults failing closed to ESCALATE with SYSTEM_FAILURE, label isolation, and snippets treated as data. Covers the model-fault part of FR-8 and AC-13.

Build the evaluation harness: every Metrics-section figure by run, framing and primary family, the run manifest, at least 3 repeated runs, cost and latency, modelled review time, and the always-escalate and always-close reference agents.

Commit the modelled-time parameters, run the baseline on the frozen world, publish the report, and commit the targets decision record required by AC-16. The gate checks the committed artifacts and does not call the model.

Reserved for wave-2 planning. Upgrades, audit log, review policy, operational mode, release protocol and README are planned in detail after the baseline. This task is rejected at the wave-2 reopen and is not meant to be completed.

controls.reason: Three independent Codex rounds. Rounds 1 and 2 found real problems (injection wording, hard-case labels, loader paths) and I had them fixed. Round 3 returned APPROVE using its own classifier on three new seeds. I accept the remaining limits (neutral-note cue, injection cue, loader-only isolation) because they are written in the design note and will be measured later.

Two independent Codex rounds ended in APPROVE after fixes. I reviewed the 50 fixed alternate wordings and the design decisions myself. The tests keep dates, identifiers and names across the three framings. I know the wording checks are keyword-based and do not prove equal agent behaviour, which T07 will measure.
